caseno: Civil Revision Case No. 297 and 298 of 1976.
lawyer:
Ahmed Sobhan with Md. Fazlul Karim, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with A.S Md. Rashed and Nizamuddin Khan, Advocates-----For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
A.K.M. Masudul Alam ----- Opp. Party.
full_judgment: 10. In a case where issues are purely of law which do not require any investigation into the facts and the Court is of opinion that the case or any part thereof may be disposed of on the issues of law only, it is incumbent upon the court to determine the issues of law first if the determination of issues of law is postponed to be determined along with the issues of fact it will, in my opinion, mean unnecessary inconvenience and expenses to the parties and waste of time and labour of the court as if on the other hand, the court is of opinion that the issues of law cannot be determined without investigation into facts or the point of law raised is not clear or that the case or any part thereof cannot be disposed of the court well. In many cases the issues of law such as on a point of limitation, res judicata jurisdiction or the suit being barred on the face of it by any law, arise and the court having regard to the facts and circumstances of the Case is of opinion that the case or any part thereof may be disposed of on such issue, the court has no option having regard to the provision of Order 14 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure but to determine those issues first. If on the other hand; the court is of opinion that the issues of law cannot be determined without investigation into facts or the point of law raised is not, clear or that the Case or any part thereof cannot be disposed of, the court may decline to determine the issues of how first. Therefore, it is the duty of the court to address itself to these vital points and then decide whether the issues of law should be decided first or they should be decided along with the issues of fact.
